name: __FORGE_SCOPE__/backend
//pinned: @nestjs/jwt and @nestjs/passport are held at 11.x DELIBERATELY. Their 12.x
releases are ESM-only ('type': 'module' in their package.json), and this
package is CommonJS: jest fails outright with "Must use import to load ES
Module" before a single test runs, and Node 22 is what CI and the Docker
images use. Upgrading means moving this package's test runner off CommonJS
first. Verified against 12.0.0, 12.0.1 and 12.0.2.
@nestjs/terminus is held at 11.x DELIBERATELY, for the same reason. Its 12.x
releases are ESM-only ('type': 'module', with only a 'default' export
condition), and this package is CommonJS: a spec that imports it fails with
"Must use import to load ES Module" before a single test runs, even on Node 26.
11.1.1 is CommonJS, and its peers (@nestjs/common,
@nestjs/core, @nestjs/typeorm at ^10 || ^11) are satisfied here. The two
versions differ in API as well: 11.x takes `pingCheck(key, { timeout })`,
where 12.x has `pingCheck(key).withTimeout(ms)`. Verified against 12.1.0.
otplib is held at 12.x DELIBERATELY, having actually tried 13.5.0 rather than
assumed it. otplib itself ships a proper dual ESM/CJS build (unlike the pin
above), so `require('otplib')` alone is fine — the break is one level
deeper: its only published Base32 plugin, @otplib/plugin-base32-scure
(13.5.0), depends on @scure/base (2.4.0), which is ESM-only ('type':
'module', a bare 'main' pointing at index.js, no 'exports' map, no .cjs
build at all) and is required EAGERLY when otplib's top-level API
(generateSync/verifySync/generateSecret/generateURI, imported from 'otplib'
itself) is first loaded, not lazily when a Base32 secret is actually
decoded. A TOTP secret is Base32 by convention (mfa_methods.totp_secret,
TotpEnrollmentOffer.secret), so there is no configuration of otplib 13's
own API that avoids this plugin. Reproduced with: `import { generateSync }
from 'otplib';` as the first line of a spec file under this package's own
jest (30.5.2) + ts-jest (29.4.14), on Node v26.10.0 (newer, and per Jest's
own error text more capable of require(esm), than the >=22 <23 this
package targets — so this is not a Node-version artifact that a pinned
Node 22 would avoid; an older runtime can only fail the same way or worse):
Must use import to load ES Module: .../node_modules/@scure/base/index.js
...Jest supports require(esm) natively [only] ... Node v24.9+
at .../@otplib/plugin-base32-scure/src/index.ts:8:39 (sourcemapped;
the code that actually ran is dist/index.cjs)
at .../otplib/src/defaults.ts:9:41 (sourcemapped; dist/index.cjs)
at TotpVerifier.spec.ts:1:1
Plain `node -e "require('otplib').generateSync(...)"` (no Jest) succeeds on
the same install, on the same Node — current Node can require(esm) a pure
ESM package directly; Jest's own CJS module registry cannot yet, which is
exactly the gap its own error message names. otplib ships no alternative
Base32 plugin package (only @otplib/plugin-base32-scure exists), so moving
off 12.x means either this package's Jest runner leaving CommonJS (the same
precondition the pin above already names), or this codebase shipping its
own Base32 codec to hand otplib's `base32` plugin option instead of the
default — which is exactly the hand-rolled, unverified-by-an-independent-
source code TotpVerifier.ts's own TSDoc argues against building here.
@simplewebauthn/server is NOT held back, and is recorded here so that stays a
choice rather than an accident: 14.0.3 (the current major) was tried under
this package's own jest and tsc (module commonjs, moduleResolution node) and
loads and runs — its 'exports' map carries a 'require' condition pointing at
a real CommonJS build (./script/index.js), unlike the two pins above. Before
raising the major, repeat that: import it from a spec and call
generateRegistrationOptions under this package's jest.
@nestjs/swagger is a plain dependency, not a devDependency, and that is
forced. Its CLI plugin (nest-cli.json) injects require("@nestjs/swagger")
into every compiled file that carries OpenAPI metadata, so the production
image needs the package at runtime even though it never serves the document;
`npm prune --omit=dev` must keep it. It brings swagger-ui-dist (~11 MB) into
that image for the same reason. Moving it to devDependencies breaks the
production image at start-up.
swagger-ui-dist depends on @scarf/scarf, whose postinstall script reports
install analytics to scarf.sh over the network (and runs `git rev-parse HEAD`
and `npm ls` to do it) unless disabled. On npm it is ON by default. The root
package.json sets "scarfSettings": { "enabled": false }, which silences it
for every `npm ci` in CI and in the Docker builds. Removing that setting
makes every install of every project generated from this template call out.
The paginated query DTOs carry @ApiPropertyOptional() on `page` and `limit`:
the plugin derives `required` from the `?` modifier, and these are declared
`page: number = 1` with @IsOptional(), so without it a client generated from
the document is told both are mandatory. That is the failure for DTOs in
*.dto.ts files, which the plugin reads. For the ones it does not match
(PaginationQueryDto in common/types/pagination.ts, and the two audit query
DTOs declared inside controller files) the decorator is what puts the
parameters in the document at all: without it they are absent.
